content: Individuals who have a history of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) should undergo regular screenings for type 2 diabetes. The frequency of these screenings typically ranges from every 1 to 3 years, depending on the presence of specific risk factors. These evaluations should include annual assessments of glucose levels or the performance of an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) to facilitate early detection of any abnormalities. Even if the initial postpartum testing results are within normal limits, it is crucial to continue regular monitoring due to the significantly increased risk of developing diabetes later in life.
